findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): account ID and login from the GitHub connection
findings.evidence: agent.js:38 matches a localized schema validation message. AgentCustomization.kt:31–34 rejects webhook URLs containing credentials. AgentCustomizationUi.kt matches the text 'guide', not a UID variable. In the actual GitHub connection, GitHubClient.kt:54–55 receives an account ID and login from GitHub after the user initiates connection. GitHubProjects.kt:49–55 keeps these identifiers in the local project state, and :66–72 compares the returned numeric ID when replacing credentials. GitHubClient.kt:182–185 sends the supplied bearer token to GitHub via HTTPS. AgentHttpTransport.kt:70,109–113 uses a separately supplied OpenRouter bearer key. These authentication credentials are distinct from the retrieved GitHub ID and login, and the traced flows do not send those returned identifiers off-device.
findings.recommendation: Review the disclosure for the optional GitHub integration and OpenRouter authentication to ensure it describes the destination and use of the credentials. Document the actual flows and independently verify the User IDs category in Play Console if another release path transmits an account identifier. https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): no web browsing history in the traced runtime
findings.evidence: agent.js:44 matches downloadUrl schema metadata, not WebView navigation. AgentCustomizationUi.kt:421 opens a user-selected skills listing in an external browser and :452 mentions the runtime origin in webhook configuration. AgentSdkRuntime.kt:187–200 blocks navigation and serves its entry and JavaScript from packaged assets. The permitted HTTPS origin requests in :193–196 are tool requests, and :219 only loads the synthetic entry URL. The history in :376–392 is an agent conversation transcript, which can reach OpenRouter through :236–247 and AgentHttpTransport.kt:109–127. No collection or transmission of a visited-sites list was found in the traced code.
findings.recommendation: Document chat history and optional web tool queries under their applicable data types. The inspected paths do not substantiate a Web browsing history declaration.

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): App performance telemetry export was not observed
findings.evidence: agent.js:44 defines status_code in OpenRouter Fusion error schemas, and agent.js:91 renders the returned HTTP status in run progress. AgentHttpTransport.kt:84,126,142 and 185 log local Android diagnostics. AgentCustomizationUi.kt:239–247 and 360–371 trigger a typed skills.sh search on user action. SkillsDirectoryClient.kt:106–117,300–304 sends the search query, limit and DNT header via HTTPS using OkHttp, with no performance metrics in the observed request. The telemetry label at AgentCustomizationUi.kt:371 describes a CLI flag rather than a telemetry API.
findings.recommendation: Assess the user-entered skills.sh search query separately as optional in-app search data under Google Play Data safety. Keep the discovery UI description aligned with the HTTPS request in SkillsDirectoryClient.

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): No dedicated race or ethnicity collection observed
findings.evidence: The race matches in agent.js:55 and 63 use Promise.race to resolve competing operations. The MiniAppGenerator.kt:36 match comes from the word gracefully in bundled rendering instructions. The inference path at MiniAppGenerator.kt:262–271 sends the system instructions and the user prompt, with no race or ethnicity field in the observed request.
findings.recommendation: Cover open-ended user prompts in the appropriate chat or user-generated-content Data safety category. The traced code provides no basis for a dedicated race or ethnicity declaration.

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): No dedicated date-of-birth or other-profile collection observed
findings.evidence: The dob substring matches in agent.js:4, 38, 40 and 79 are Zod object identifiers or the Czech localization text for duration. There is no literal dob field or date-of-birth source in the matched code.
findings.recommendation: Cover open-ended prompts and documents under their applicable Data safety categories. The traced patterns provide no evidence of a dedicated personal profile payload.

findings.issue_summary: User-Initiated Collection: Project-file upload can include existing voice or sound recordings
findings.evidence: agent.js:38,40,48,50,51 and 95 uses record for data structures or agent behavior, and agent.js:44 contains SDK input_audio schemas without a matching native audio capture path. MiniAppActivity.kt:676 denies WebView permission requests. Separately, ProjectFilesUi.kt:277 accepts any system-picker MIME type and :255–260 offers an explicit Upload to OpenRouter action. MainActivity.kt:773–774 and :788–793 wire these to OpenRouterFiles.kt:45–49 and :56–61, which copy the full selected file bytes. OpenRouterAgentClient.kt:117–136 posts those bytes as multipart application/octet-stream to the OpenRouter Files API, with the user's Bearer key at :248. Those bytes can include a user-selected recording.
findings.recommendation: Verify the Data safety declaration and privacy policy cover optional project-file uploads, including voice or sound recordings where applicable, and retain accurate file types, purpose, retention and deletion disclosures. Google Play treats off-device transmission as collection, while a specific and reasonably expected user-initiated action can qualify for an exemption from the sharing declaration. See https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469?hl=en

findings.issue_summary: User-Initiated Collection: The optional file upload can transmit user-selected music files
findings.evidence: The scanner hits in agent.js:40, 47, 53, 55, 78 refer to tracking tool work or generating an app, and BackgroundRuns.kt:40, 50, 212, 243 tracks run lifecycle. MiniAppGenerator.kt:35 suggests synthesized Web Audio and a JavaScript music library. None of those hits reads a user's music. The actual path is ProjectFilesUi.kt:119, 255–260, 275–278: the Android picker accepts */* and a separate Upload to OpenRouter button sends the selected project file. OpenRouterFiles.kt:56–62, 128–129 copies raw bytes. OpenRouterAgentClient.kt:71, 117–136 posts those bytes and the filename to OpenRouter's HTTPS Files API without a client-side media type filter. OpenRouter documents that uploads are stored under the authenticating API key's workspace. A live music upload was not performed.
findings.recommendation: Include Music files as optional collection for App functionality if audio/music uploads remain supported in the release. Verify backend file-type restrictions and whether any model-provider transfer meets Google's sharing exceptions. See [Play Data safety guidance](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469?hl=en) and [OpenRouter Files API](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/files/upload-file).

findings.issue_summary: User-Initiated Collection: OpenRouter receives project files and associated names
findings.evidence: ProjectFilesUi.kt:255–260 starts a labeled upload. OpenRouterFiles.kt:56–62, 128–129 reads the selected file and OpenRouterAgentClient.kt:71, 117–136 POSTs its filename and bytes as multipart data to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/files using the user's key. AgentSdkRuntime.kt:398–399 also supplies selected file IDs and names to the agent request for attachments. The text/plain scanner hits at AgentSdkRuntime.kt:226 and MiniAppActivity.kt:270–275 construct empty local error responses. The localStorage hit at agent.js:78 tells the model to persist mini-app state locally. MiniAppActivity.kt:99–100, 158–163 isolates origin storage and blocks device-file access. Network-enabled generated mini apps can make HTTPS requests (MiniAppGenerator.kt:115, MiniAppActivity.kt:218–222), but the localStorage hint alone does not establish a concrete document payload. The separate MiniAppActivity.kt:482–500 transfer is an explicit Android Sharesheet export.
findings.recommendation: Declare Files and docs collection as optional for App functionality. Cover uploaded content and filenames, the OpenRouter workspace, attachment processing by model providers, and retention/deletion in the privacy policy. Determine the sharing answer using Google's service-provider and expected user-action exceptions and the actual provider arrangements. See [Play Data safety guidance](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469?hl=en) and [OpenRouter privacy policy](https://openrouter.ai/privacy/).

findings.issue_summary: Silent Background Transfer — Google Play services LiteRT metrics are absent from the moderation explanation.
findings.evidence: Moderation is off by default. Once a user enables it, the app initializes Google Play services LiteRT when settings are saved and during later app startup with that preference. Google's SDK documentation states that the device identifier, device and app information, API events, error codes, and performance and utilization metrics are sent to Google. User prompts and responses processed by this SDK stay on device. The setting describes only local prompt and response checks, so selecting it gives no notice of the SDK's metrics transfer. The scanner's ActivityManager match uses TaskDescription to set a Recents label/icon on device. The bundled agent's trace match is an optional request schema property and the app does not populate it. AgentHttpTransport diagnostics are written to logcat.
findings.recommendation: Include optional Diagnostics and Device or other IDs in the Play Console Data safety review and describe the SDK's diagnostics and usage analytics in the app privacy policy. Explain Google's SDK metrics before enabling moderation or initializing the SDK and obtain informed opt-in if continuing to use this runtime. Verify the precise collection and sharing answers against the SDK's terms. See https://developers.google.com/edge/litert/android/play_services#privacy_and_data_collection and https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10144311.

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only) — The flagged GitHub field is a repository path.
findings.evidence: GitHubClient reads full_name from the repository API response as its owner/repository path. It uses that path to address the selected repository on GitHub. The account API separately reads id and login. The scanner's full_name signal does not establish access to or transmission of someone's personal name.
findings.recommendation: Exclude the repository full_name field as evidence of the Name category. Evaluate actual account identifiers separately.

findings.issue_summary: Manual Sharing — Gallery icon photos stay on device until export or share, and photos can be selected for OpenRouter upload.
findings.evidence: Android's photo picker grants access to a chosen icon photo, which is resized and saved to the app's private mini app folder. The gallery picker and icon save do not upload it. An explicit mini app export or share includes the icon PNG in the archive and writes it to the user's chosen document provider or grants the chosen Sharesheet app temporary read access. Separately, the generic file picker accepts any file type. If the user later selects Upload to OpenRouter for a photo file in that workspace, the app sends it as multipart content via the OpenRouter Files API.
findings.recommendation: Call out the bundled icon photo in the share or export UI. Treat reasonably expected, user-initiated transfers using the applicable sharing exception. Account for optional Photos collection when user-selected photo files are sent to OpenRouter. The sharing exemption does not remove the off-device collection analysis. See https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469.

findings.issue_summary: The mobile app targets API 35 and cannot meet the API 36 submission requirement
findings.evidence: The default configuration sets targetSdk to 35 and compileSdk to 35. The checked-in debug APK also reports target API 35. Google Play requires API 36 or later for new mobile apps and updates starting August 31, 2026. The announced extension ended November 1, 2026.
findings.recommendation: Raise compileSdk and targetSdk to at least 36, test the Android 16 behavior changes, and confirm the target SDK in the release artifact before submission. [Google Play target API level requirements](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878)

findings.issue_summary: Verify the Play Console declaration for the dataSync foreground service
findings.evidence: AgentRunService declares dataSync with the required permission. Starting a user-requested agent run starts the service, which preserves the active network response stream while the app is backgrounded. The ongoing notification shows progress and includes Stop. Run completion stops the service. This fits the stated server-side processing example. Play Console declaration status remains unverified.
findings.recommendation: Declare dataSync under App content, describe how deferring or interrupting the stream affects the user, and attach a video showing the user starting a run, backgrounding the app, and stopping it from the ongoing notification. [Google Play foreground service requirements](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13392821)

findings.issue_summary: Core chat requires an OpenRouter credential; verify reviewer access in Play Console
findings.evidence: The app can open without a credential, but AgentViewModel.send returns before starting a run when no OpenRouter API key is stored. Settings accepts a pasted key or starts the OpenRouter browser flow. Optional GitHub integration requires a fine-grained token. Play Console App access instructions and reviewer credentials were unavailable for verification.
findings.recommendation: In Play Console under App content > App access, provide a dedicated reusable, non-expiring reviewer OpenRouter key with a working model and sufficient quota. Include English instructions to paste the key in Settings, save it, choose a model and send a test prompt. Supply a disposable test repository and suitable credentials for any gated GitHub feature included in review. Verify all reviewer steps on a fresh install. See https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/15748846.

findings.issue_summary: Confirm Data safety account-creation answers for the OpenRouter connection
findings.evidence: Settings links to OpenRouter key management and starts browser authorization at OpenRouter. The exchange obtains a user-controlled OpenRouter API key and the app stores that key locally with Android Keystore. The optional GitHub connection also uses an externally issued credential. The audited app paths exposed no developer-managed app-account creation flow. Play also considers creation of an app-specific identity through an external signup flow to be account creation.
findings.recommendation: Complete the Data safety deletion questions using the actual production sign-up flow. If the release provisions an app-specific account through OpenRouter or any other service, provide a discoverable in-app path and a public web resource for requesting deletion of the app account and associated data. Document which data users can delete locally and how they can manage retained OpenRouter files and account data. See https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13327111 and https://openrouter.ai/privacy.
